header.name: Design Thinking and Innovation
offered_to:
1. B.Tech Pre-final Year students
2. B.Tech Final year students
3. Pre-Final year M.Tech students
(UG/PG)
header.description: Design Thinking has been recognized the world over as an important skill to successfully harness the power of non-linear, creative and empathetic approaches. Professional success in the past has largely been about replicating prior period successes into a relatively similar and predictable future. Therefore education around the world has focused on linear, analytical, and sequential thinking. However, the present we are operating in, and the future we are heading into is going to be significantly different from the past that we have come from. It is going to be more uncertain, unpredictable, and exponential, resulting in greater complexity along with exponential opportunities and exponential organizations. While logical, linear, analytical and sequential thinking will continue to be required it will not be sufficient to thrive in this future. Individuals and organizations will also need to adopt non-linear, intuitive, empathetic and creative thinking to succeed in this uncertain future. A whole new way of thinking will be required.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: To comprehend the changing social, technological and business environment and role and relevance of Design Thinking

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: To develop capability to frame and reframe problems and analyse emerging context

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: To develop a creative, empathetic, outcome oriented and iterative approach to finding innovative solutions to problems

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: To develop an innovative mindset by applying learning to a specific problem and translating that into a feasible technology based solution design

lecture_topics: Introduction to Design Thinking – The Art of framing problem
The Art of Framing and Reframing problem statements and developing Design Briefs
Understanding problems as a part of larger systems
Developing an empathetic approach to problems
